Create higher-level library crate for app integrations (over kyz-core)
description:
Add a stable higher-level library crate (name TBD: `kyz-runtime`, `kyz-resolver`, or `kyz-integration`) that applications can link against directly instead of shelling out to `kyz-cli`.

Problem
- `kyz-core` is a good primitive layer but is too low-level for consumers like Oqto.
- CLI integration is brittle (stdout parsing, process orchestration, awkward unlock/session handling).
- We need a reusable, non-Oqto-specific app integration surface.

Requirements
- Thin abstraction over `kyz-core`, not a second policy engine.
- No Oqto-specific concepts in public API.
- Async-friendly where relevant, but do not force async for pure local operations.
- Clear error taxonomy for: locked vault, missing entry, ambiguous ref, unsupported kind, expired session, keyring unavailable.

Proposed API surface
- open default/explicit vault
- attach to existing unlock session
- query unlock status
- list entry metadata without secret values
- resolve entries by ref / selector
- layered resolve helpers (to be provided by child issue)
- typed helpers for common kinds (ssh key, token, basic auth, api key)

Deliverables
- New crate with public API docs and examples.
- One integration example showing local app usage without CLI subprocesses.
- Guidance on when to use `kyz-core` vs the higher-level crate.

Definition of done
- A consumer like Oqto can resolve/list secrets entirely through library calls.
- No CLI subprocess is required for local integration.
- Public API is generic and useful outside Oqto.

title: Add brokered scoped-session API to avoid vault passphrase in child env
description:
Add a brokered/scoped-session access mode so wrapped processes and app integrations do not need `KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD` or equivalent raw unlock material in their environment.

Problem
- Current `kyz exec` path injects `KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD` into the child env.
- That is acceptable for some CLI workflows but too weak as a trust boundary for agent/harness integrations.
- We need scoped access where the child gets a lease/token/socket, not the vault passphrase.

Requirements
- Support issuing short-lived scoped handles for a subset of refs/capabilities.
- Handle expiry, revocation, and bounded use-count cleanly.
- Work for local same-machine integrations first.
- Be compatible with future headless/remote auth flows.
- Avoid requiring HTTP if a local Unix socket / in-process broker is cleaner.

Possible designs to evaluate
- Unix socket broker with per-session handle
- Opaque bearer token mapped to scoped lease in memory
- In-process broker object for direct library consumers

Must not do
- Re-introduce child-visible vault passphrases under a new name.
- Hardcode Oqto policy concepts into kyz.

Deliverables
- Design doc comparing broker/token/socket shapes.
- Initial implementation of one brokered access path.
- Migration plan for `kyz exec` / wrapped workflows.

Definition of done
- A wrapped child can resolve/use allowed secrets without receiving vault passphrase material.
- Scope is enforced by broker/session boundary.
- This works as a generic kyz feature, not only for Oqto.

title: Add first-class SSH identity metadata and listing helpers
description:
Add first-class support for SSH identity discovery/metadata so consumers can safely list and select SSH-capable entries without manually parsing arbitrary secret payloads.

Important boundary
- Metadata must be optional.
- kyz must remain useful standalone with generic secrets.
- Oqto-specific policy (allowed hosts, session grants, approval modes) stays outside kyz.

Problem
- SSH-first integrations need a safe way to enumerate candidate identities.
- Consumers should not need to deserialize arbitrary blobs just to discover fingerprints/public keys/comments.
- Today this likely has to be reconstructed ad hoc outside kyz.

Requirements
- Support an SSH-oriented kind/annotation model that is optional.
- Expose metadata without exposing private key material.
- Helpers should derive and/or validate:
  - public key
  - fingerprint
  - algorithm
  - comment/label (optional)
- Work with entries that omit metadata by deriving where possible.

Possible shape
- typed entry kind `ssh_key`
- optional metadata map for label/comment/tags
- helper APIs like `list_ssh_identities()` and `ssh_identity_metadata(ref)`

Deliverables
- Schema/API proposal for optional SSH metadata.
- Library helpers for listing SSH-capable entries safely.
- Tests for entries with explicit metadata and entries with derived metadata.

Definition of done
- Integrators can enumerate SSH identities without reading/decrypting unnecessary data into app-specific parsing layers.
- Metadata remains optional and generic.

title: Add layered resolver API for workspace-first / personal-fallback lookups
description:
Add a reusable layered resolver API so applications can resolve refs across multiple vault sources without re-implementing precedence logic themselves.

Problem
- Integrations like Oqto need a predictable lookup model: workspace vault first, personal/user vault fallback.
- This pattern is generally useful and should live in a reusable library layer, not be duplicated in every consumer.
- Consumers also need to know which source won for policy and UX purposes.

Requirements
- Resolve against ordered sources/layers.
- Return both resolved entry and source provenance.
- Support explicit constraints like workspace-only or personal-only.
- Distinguish not-found from ambiguous/conflicting results.
- Keep the API generic (not Oqto-specific naming in public surface).

Example use cases
- project deploy key in workspace vault overrides user default
- user token fallback when workspace has no matching entry
- headless service mode forbids personal fallback entirely

Deliverables
- Resolver API and source provenance model.
- Tests for precedence, ambiguity, not-found, and source-constrained lookups.
- Docs/examples for multi-vault consumers.

Definition of done
- A consumer can express ordered vault resolution without custom glue code.
- Result carries enough provenance for the caller to apply its own policy.

title: Formalize headless unlock modes and service-friendly lifecycle semantics
description:
Formalize headless unlock behavior so applications and operators can reason clearly about workstation, headless service, and remote approval modes.

Problem
- kyz already has useful pieces (vault sessions, keyring/keyutils-backed unlock state, headless auth request flow), but the operational model is still implicit.
- Integrators need a documented and supported story for when auto-unlock is acceptable, when interactive unlock is required, and how unlock state behaves over runner/service restarts.

Requirements
- Define supported unlock modes, at minimum:
  1. interactive personal unlock
  2. machine/service unlock for non-personal vaults
  3. remote approval/unlock flow
  4. locked-but-requestable state
- Clarify security properties and tradeoffs of each mode.
- Clarify Linux headless behavior with keyutils/session storage and machine-bound fallback.
- Provide guidance for multi-vault setups (workspace/service vault vs personal vault).

Deliverables
- Design doc / docs update covering unlock modes and lifecycle.
- Minimal API/CLI adjustments if needed to surface mode explicitly.
- Recommendations for integrators deciding which mode to use.

Definition of done
- Headless/service operators have a clear supported unlock story.
- App integrators do not need to reverse-engineer expected behavior from implementation details.

title: Explore direct SSH signing API for kyz-managed identities
description:
Research and, if feasible, prototype a direct signing API for SSH-capable identities so applications can request signatures without handling raw private key material beyond the kyz boundary.

Why
- Longer-term integrations may want a kyz-managed SSH signer instead of depending on the user's ambient ssh-agent.
- This is especially relevant for service/workspace keys and future brokered SSH mediation.

Scope
- Evaluate key format support and library choices.
- Define whether signing lives in `kyz-core` or the higher-level integration crate.
- Keep API generic and not Oqto-specific.
- Explicitly document whether this is in-memory-only, broker-backed, or both.

Non-goal
- Do not block the first SSH MVP on this issue.

Definition of done
- We have a concrete recommendation (implement now, defer, or reject) with enough detail for a follow-up implementation issue.

title: Remote auth flow for headless agent secret access
description:
Design and implement remote/headless auth flow for agent secret access that is secure and ergonomic (low approval fatigue).

Goals
- Keep raw secrets out of agent env/files whenever possible.
- Support temporary scoped approvals (leases) without requiring agent process restarts for mediated capabilities.
- Provide strong auditability and revocation while minimizing approval nags.

Scope
1) Approval lease model
   - lease fields: actor/session/process, capability, target (host/path/secret_ref), ttl, max_uses, risk_tier.
   - grant modes: once, session, timed (e.g. 15m/1h).
   - deterministic expiry and revocation semantics.
2) Policy and anti-nag ergonomics
   - risk-tiered prompts (low-risk auto+audit, high-risk explicit).
   - host-group and capability presets to avoid repeated prompts.
   - process allowlist integration for trusted executables.
3) SSH mediation compatibility
   - support ssh-wrapper flow where agent uses normal ssh alias commands while real key material remains inaccessible.
   - alias resolution in trusted layer; per-host approval and audit events.
4) Observability
   - structured events for request/grant/deny/use/expire/revoke.

Definition of done
- Headless/agent flows can request secrets with scoped leases.
- Approval prompts are bounded and non-spammy under normal workflows.
- All approvals and uses are auditable and revocable.
- SSH mediated flow works with aliases and no key exposure to agents.

pi-kyz extension: automatic secret injection and scrubbing for pi agents
description:
Create a pi extension for kyz that provides automatic secret injection and output scrubbing for AI agent sessions.

## Core features
1. **bash env injection** — override built-in bash tool, inject vault secrets as env vars via spawnHook
2. **output scrubbing** — tool_result event scrubs secret values from ALL tool output (bash, read, grep, etc.)
3. **system prompt injection** — before_agent_start adds available secret names so LLM knows to use $SECRET_NAME
4. **user bash injection** — user_bash event injects secrets into ! commands too
5. **/kyz command** — lists secret names (never values)
6. **/kyz-set command** — set a secret from within pi session

## Advanced features (beyond baseline)
1. **Use kyz exec/pipe model** — don't load all secrets into every bash env. Use kyz's policy engine to scope which secrets are available per command. Prefer targeted injection over blanket injection.
2. **Auth request flow** — leverage kyz's auth_request system. When the agent needs a secret not pre-approved, the extension can show an approval prompt via ctx.ui.confirm() that feeds back into kyz's approval/lease model.
3. **Policy-aware scrubbing** — scrub based on what the policy says is sensitive, not just vault contents. Also scrub partial matches (base64-encoded variants, URL-encoded, etc.).
4. **Wrap mode** — support kyz wrap semantics: pre-approve a set of secrets at session start, block kyz get inside the session.
5. **Tag-based scoping** — /kyz-scope tag:aws to limit which secrets are injected (uses kyz's existing tag system).
6. **Audit events** — feed tool_call events into kyz's audit log so there's a record of which agent session used which secrets.

## Integration surface: CLI only
pi has no native MCP support. The extension shells out to kyz-cli:
- 'kyz list --json' to enumerate secret names
- 'kyz get --json service/key' to retrieve values for scrubbing
- 'kyz exec --env ...' semantics via spawnHook env injection
- All kyz commands must be on PATH

## Implementation notes
- Extension lives in byteowlz/pi-agent-extensions/pi-kyz/
- Depends on kyz-cli binary being on PATH
- Use child_process.execSync/spawn for kyz CLI calls
- Cache secret names at session start, refresh on /kyz-reload
- Secret values loaded lazily for scrubbing, cached in memory with TTL

## Open questions
- Blanket injection vs on-demand (kyz exec model) vs hybrid?
- Should the extension auto-discover workspace .kyz/ vaults?

title: Audit log facility: record secret access/injection events to a queryable sink
description:
## Problem

kyz currently has no audit mechanism — no `audit` subcommand, and nothing in
kyz-core/kyz-runtime records secret access, injection, or set/get events.

This surfaced via the `pi-kyz` agent extension, whose `kyzAudit()` helper was
written to "log audit event via kyz exec dry-run" but, lacking any real sink,
just does `process.stderr.write("[kyz] ...")`. In headless runs (`pi -p`) those
lines leak straight into stdout/stderr alongside agent output. There is nothing
in kyz for it to feed into.

## Proposal

Add a first-class audit log so wrappers/extensions/MCP have a real sink:

- Append-only JSONL at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/kyz/audit.log` (alongside vault.json),
  rotated/size-capped. Each record: `{ ts, op, service?, key?, actor?, session?, detail? }`.
- Emit events from the natural choke points already in the runtime:
  `get`, `set`, `delete`, `exec`/`wrap` injection, `ipc` grants.
- `kyz audit` subcommand to query/tail (`--json`, `--since`, `--service`, `--op`),
  consistent with `history`/`log`/`events` ergonomics.
- Off-by-default or config-gated (`audit.enabled` in config.toml) to avoid
  surprising plaintext-on-disk for users who don't want it. Never record values.

## Why

- Gives `kyz wrap`/MCP/agent integrations a proper audit trail instead of each
  caller inventing ad-hoc stderr logging.
- Unblocks the pi-kyz extension fix: route `kyzAudit()` to this sink (or drop its
  own logging entirely) instead of writing to stderr.

## Related

- Consumer: pi-agent-extensions/pi-kyz (stderr-leak bug to be fixed once a sink exists)

description:
Goal: secure secret submission and brokered just-in-time delivery for runner execution contexts (local + remote) without bulk vault replication.

Refined direction (least privilege + layered security):
- No full-vault copy/sync to remote runner hosts.
- Secrets are delivered only when needed, for a specific approved operation.
- Use brokered one-time grants with strict scope and expiry.

Scope:
1) Local IPC endpoint for one-time secret submission requests.
   - Unix socket with owner-only permissions.
   - Payload: request_id, service, key, value/envelope, expires_at, origin metadata.
   - Replay protection for request_id + TTL enforcement.

2) Brokered JIT grant model (foundation for remote runners).
   - Grant token includes: allowed secret ref(s), command/workspace constraints, ttl, use_count.
   - Runner-side consumer validates grant before resolving secret.
   - Default behavior is non-persistent injection (stdin/env for child process only).

3) Audit + safety.
   - Log only metadata (request_id/service/key/outcome/scope), never secret values.
   - Explicit denial reasons for expired, replayed, out-of-scope, unauthorized.

Acceptance criteria:
- Endpoint accepts valid one-time requests and stores/resolves correctly.
- Secret values never appear in logs/stdout/stderr/diagnostics payloads.
- Replay and expiry are enforced.
- Socket access is restricted to intended local user/process context.
- Grant validation rejects out-of-scope command/workspace usage.
- Tests cover happy path, replay, expiry, malformed payload, scope violation.

kyz get latency (~2s/secret) causes blocking in pi-kyz extension
description:
Observed while benchmarking pi first-prompt latency with kyz vault unlocked.

Findings (local timings):
- `kyz vault status --json`: ~1.09s
- `kyz list --json`: ~0.004s
- `kyz get --json --service <svc> <key>`: ~2.1s per call

Impact:
- Extensions/integrations that call `kyz get` for multiple secrets synchronously can add several seconds of startup/first-turn delay.
- In pi-kyz, this manifested as first prompt appearing to hang before being sent.

Repro steps:
1. Unlock kyz vault.
2. Time commands repeatedly:
   - `kyz vault status --json`
   - `kyz list --json`
   - `kyz get --json --service <svc> <key>`
3. Observe `get` is consistently ~2s while list is near-instant.

Expected:
- `kyz get` should be significantly faster for unlocked vault (ideally << 500ms), or provide an efficient bulk retrieval API to avoid N per-secret roundtrips.

Potential directions:
- Add/optimize bulk read endpoint/command (e.g. get-many/list-with-values for trusted local use).
- Improve cache/reuse of unlocked vault/session state for repeated `get`.
- Profile crypto/disk/process overhead inside `kyz get` path.

Related downstream symptom:
- pi extension latency spikes when injecting/scrubbing secrets from vault in hot paths.

auth-request flow: approved secrets stealable via unauthenticated one-time pickup URL
description:
## Summary

The kyz-api auth-request flow delivers human-approved secrets to whoever GETs /auth/secrets/{id} first. The stash is keyed ONLY by the request ID — no requester binding, no capability token. With KYZ_API_TOKEN unset (the DEFAULT deployment), auth_middleware passes every request, and GET /auth/request publicly lists ALL request IDs + scopes.

## Attack (dynamically confirmed against a local build, v0.7.0)

Attacker = any principal that can open TCP to 127.0.0.1:<port>: another local Unix user on a shared host, any co-located container sharing the netns (k8s pod sidecars), or a web page in the user's browser (CORS allow_origin(Any), subject to browser PNA):

1. GET /auth/request -> harvest pending request IDs + scopes (no auth)
2. websocat ws://127.0.0.1:3000/auth/wait/<id> -> notified the instant a human approves
3. human approves: POST /auth/approve/{id} with vault passphrase (only human action)
4. attacker GET /auth/secrets/{id} -> one-time pickup returns FULL plaintext values
5. legitimate requester's pickup -> 404 (stash consumed by attacker)

Observed: attacker received {"github/token":{"value":"ghp_SUPERSECRETVALUE123"}} without ever knowing the passphrase.

## Affected code

- crates/kyz-api/src/main.rs:147-156 (auth_middleware: no token -> pass all)
- crates/kyz-api/src/main.rs:221 (list_auth_requests: lists IDs/scopes unauthenticated)
- crates/kyz-api/src/main.rs:429-440 (pickup_secrets: no caller check)
- crates/kyz-core/src/auth_request.rs:143 (stash_secrets), :156 (pickup_secrets: remove-by-id)

Baseline: HashiCorp Vault response wrapping returns the single-use wrap token ONLY to the requester and never lists it; Teleport binds approval to the requesting identity. Bearer-URL pickup with a public listing is a deviation.

## Remediation

1. Add a client-generated high-entropy pickup capability (>=32 bytes) to CreateAuthRequest; store alongside the request; pickup_secrets(id, capability) removes the stash only on constant-time capability match — the ID alone is never sufficient.
2. Update kyz-cli submit_and_wait_auth_request (main.rs:2031-2036, 2090-2093) in the SAME change to generate the capability client-side and send it on pickup, or legit `kyz exec` headless flow breaks.
3. Stop listing request IDs to unauthenticated callers (or require the API token for GET /auth/request even in no-token mode).
4. Consider enabling bearer auth by default for everything except /health.

## Proof of positive outcome (tests to write and run)

- Unit test (kyz-core auth_request): create request with pickup_capability; pickup with wrong capability -> Err/None (stash retained or 401); pickup with correct capability -> values; second pickup -> None. Capability must NOT appear in any list() output.
- Integration test (kyz-api): spin up router with test state, POST /auth/request without capability -> 400 (or require field); with capability -> 201; GET /auth/secrets/{id} without capability -> 401; with wrong capability -> 401; with correct -> 200 + values; repeat -> 404.
- CLI integration test: headless exec flow (`kyz exec` with locked vault + KYZ_API_URL pointing at test server) completes end-to-end with capability auth (no regression).
- Manual repro of the original attack MUST now fail: list -> wait -> pickup returns 401 without the capability.

Related: trx-ymjw (audit log for auth requests/approvals), trx-gber (request expiry/cleanup).

title: kyz wrap exports vault master passphrase into wrapped child environment (KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD)
description:
## Summary

handle_wrap (crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:2446-2449) builds the wrapped child's environment via scrubbed_env() — which strips KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD — and then EXPLICITLY re-adds it: `child_env.push(("KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD".to_string(), passphrase))`. The wrapped process (the semi-trusted agent that kyz wrap exists to scope via --allow) can read the vault MASTER passphrase from its own env (os.environ, /proc/self/environ). It is inherited by every descendant and leaks into crash dumps / env-logging integrations.

## Impact (dynamically confirmed, v0.7.0)

`kyz wrap --allow github/token -- sh -c 'echo [$KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD]'` printed the full master passphrase. The passphrase decrypts the vault file OFFLINE and PERMANENTLY (backups, synced/git-committed workspace vaults) — strictly more powerful than the session DK the child legitimately holds. The vault is already unlocked before spawn (main.rs:2426, session DK in OS keyring), so the child never needs the passphrase for its approved access — the exposure is gratuitous. Baseline: aws-vault exec / op run / Vault Agent inject scoped revocable material, never the master credential.

## Affected code

- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:2449 (the re-add)
- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:2446 (scrubbed_env — defeated)
- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:2418-2423 (non-TTY passphrase read from env — the only legit consumer)

## Remediation

Delete line 2449. Nested kyz get/exec/set inside the wrap use the persisted session (keyring DK), not the passphrase. The ONLY functionality lost is a nested non-TTY `kyz wrap` (handle_wrap's own env read at :2421) — migrate that to a `kyz unlock --from-keyring` style helper if needed. Keep scrubbed_env() as the only source of child KYZ_* vars. Design direction already tracked in trx-2c3j.2 (brokered scoped-session API) — this fix is the immediate stopgap, independent of the broker design.

## Proof of positive outcome (tests to write and run)

- Integration test: run `kyz wrap --allow svc/key -- sh -c 'env'` (or printenv via a policy-allowed wrapper); assert KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD is ABSENT from child env; assert the wrapped command can still read the allowed secret via `kyz exec/pipe` (session-based path works).
- Regression test for non-TTY wrap: KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD=<pw> kyz wrap ... still works (env read at :2421 unchanged) but does NOT propagate the variable to grandchildren.
- Manual repro of the attack MUST fail: wrapped process printing its environ shows no vault passphrase.

title: kyz exec: secret field names become injected env var names, enabling LD_PRELOAD/PATH code execution
description:
## Summary

resolve_exec_env (crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:1868-1875) and resolve_exec_env_headless (main.rs:2177-2178) convert each secret FIELD NAME to uppercase and inject it as an env var NAME=VALUE into the exec'd child (Command envs(&env) applied LAST at main.rs:2243-2247, overriding the scrubbed parent env). Field names have no allowlist/denylist — dynamic-loader and shell-hook variables (LD_PRELOAD, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, PATH, BASH_ENV, ...) are accepted. Policy checks (handle_exec:2230) inspect only the program basename, args, and --secret names — never the injected env var names; --tag/--alias-resolved entries escape even the secret-name check.

## Attack (dynamically confirmed, v0.7.0)

Poisoning primitive: a wrapped agent can `kyz set` (KYZ_NO_READ only gates get/export, main.rs:930/:1364) and `kyz import` deserializes untrusted JSON straight into SecretEntry with no field-name validation and no gate.

1. attacker: gcc -shared -fPIC -o /tmp/evil.so evil.c   (constructor payload)
2. attacker: kyz set ld --service pwn -f LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/evil.so
   (or: kyz set payload --service pwn -f PATH=/tmp/evilbin with a trojaned `id`)
3. victim: kyz exec --secret pwn/ld -- /bin/date
   -> "LD_PRELOAD constructor executed in child" (date never ran)
   victim: kyz exec --secret pwn/payload -- id -> attacker's script ran instead of /bin/id

--tag-based aliases mean the victim need not name the poisoned secret. Impact: arbitrary code execution in the user's exec context, where the vault session, keyring, and KYZ_API_TOKEN are reachable.

## Affected code

- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:1871-1875 (to_uppercase injection, interactive)
- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:2177-2178 (same, headless)
- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:2243-2247 (sink: envs(&env).exec())
- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs handle_import:1406-1445 (ungated entry vector)

## Remediation

Allowlist env var names, checked on the UPPERACASED name: ^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$ plus a hard denylist (LD_*, DYLD_*, PATH, BASH_ENV, ENV, PYTHONSTARTUP, PYTHONPATH, IFS, ...). Apply the identical filter in resolve_exec_env_headless. Alternatively/in addition, require explicit `--env NAME=svc/key:field` mappings for every injected variable instead of deriving names from field names. Defense in depth: validate field names at `kyz set` and `kyz import` time.

## Proof of positive outcome (tests to write and run)

- Unit test on the new name filter: LD_PRELOAD, ld_preload, PATH, BASH_ENV, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, IFS -> rejected; VALUE, API_KEY, DB_HOST_1 -> accepted.
- Integration test: create secret with fields PATH=/tmp/x and LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/x and NOTE=ok; run `kyz exec --secret ... -- env` via a policy-allowed wrapper; assert PATH and LD_PRELOAD are NOT set in child (or exec hard-errors), NOTE=ok IS set.
- Same test through the headless path (KYZ_API_URL test server).
- Import test: `kyz import` of JSON with an LD_PRELOAD field name -> rejected with a clear error (or warnings), benign import unchanged.
- Manual repro of both original payloads MUST no longer achieve code execution.

title: wrap --allow scoping unenforced: KYZ_NO_READ trivially bypassable, KYZ_POLICY dead code
description:
## Summary

kyz wrap's runtime scoping rests on two environment variables, both ineffective:

1. KYZ_NO_READ=1 (main.rs:2453) is consulted ONLY by handle_get (main.rs:930) and handle_export (main.rs:1364). The wrapped process controls its own environment: `env -u KYZ_NO_READ kyz export` returns full plaintext of the entire (already unlocked) vault. set/delete/list/history/rollback/pipe/exec are never gated at all.
2. KYZ_POLICY (main.rs:2463) points at a generated temp policy file but is NEVER READ anywhere in the workspace (single occurrence repo-wide). resolve_policy (kyz-core/src/policy.rs:255-269) consults only --policy and cwd/workspace/XDG discovery. Wiring it up would not help either: build_wrap_policy (main.rs:2500-2514) emits empty SecretPolicy entries which check_secret_command treats as unrestricted, and a command policy cannot restrict READS anyway. Also `--allow '*'` (main.rs:2457-2459) skips policy generation entirely.

Net effect: `kyz wrap --allow X` performs existence checks on X, unlocks the whole vault, exports the master passphrase (see trx-s7g3), and enforces nothing at runtime. The README's best-effort disclaimer covers the policy engine's command blocking — not the advertised scoping claim ("Enforce no-read mode", default true).

## Attack (dynamically confirmed, v0.7.0)

KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD='...' kyz wrap --allow github/token -- sh -c 'env -u KYZ_NO_READ kyz export'
-> full plaintext export of all secrets in the vault (aws/creds, github/token, ...)

## Remediation

Enforce scoping in an authority the child cannot mutate: create a per-wrap scoped session/grant (allowlist of refs + TTL, random session id held in process memory) that kyz-core enforces inside VaultStore::get/list/export. Drop env-var-based enforcement entirely; delete the dead KYZ_POLICY code (do not wire it up — see above). Consider gating set/import/history/rollback consistently if write-scoping is intended. Design direction tracked in trx-2c3j.2 (brokered scoped-session API); this is the concrete enforcement gap behind it.

## Proof of positive outcome (tests to write and run)

- Core test: scoped session allowing only svc/a -> get(svc/a) OK; get(svc/b) -> scoped-denied error; list/export filtered to the allowlist.
- Integration test: `kyz wrap --allow github/token -- sh -c 'env -u KYZ_NO_READ kyz get aws/creds --service aws'` -> denied by the scoped session (NOT by the removable env var); `kyz get github/token` via exec/pipe still works.
- Test that deleting/renaming the env var inside the child has no effect on enforcement.
- `--allow '*'` case: document and test that it unlocks full read by design (explicit opt-in), not accidentally.

title: vault unlock: attacker-crafted KDF params (log_n/p) from vault file cause 1TiB allocation abort (DoS)
description:
## Summary

KdfParams (crates/kyz-core/src/vault_v3.rs:71-75) deserializes log_n: u8 and p: u32 straight from the vault file. scrypt_params (vault_v3.rs:105-114) applies no application-level bound before ScryptParams::new. Workspace vaults live at <repo>/.kyz/vault.json — attacker-controlled in a malicious cloned repo. When the victim runs `kyz vault unlock` there (ANY passphrase), derive_kek (vault_v3.rs:421-434) calls scrypt with attacker-chosen parameters.

## Impact (dynamically confirmed, v0.7.0)

log_n=30 / r=8 -> scrypt working area 128*8*2^30 = 1 TiB -> "memory allocation of 1099511627776 bytes failed" -> SIGABRT (exit 134). Without ulimits: OOM-killer pressure. Crash-DoS only. NOT a crypto downgrade: kdf params feed the KEK that AEAD-unwraps wrapped_dk — altering them on an existing vault makes unwrap_dk fail (AEAD tag check), so no offline brute-force speedup is reachable.

Repro: craft {"version":3,"kdf":{"algo":"scrypt","log_n":30,"r":8,"p":1,"salt_b64":"..."},"wrapped_dk":"...","entries":{}} at <repo>/.kyz/vault.json; cd repo; kyz vault unlock; enter any passphrase.

## Affected code

- crates/kyz-core/src/vault_v3.rs:71-75 (unvalidated log_n/p from file)
- crates/kyz-core/src/vault_v3.rs:105-114 (scrypt_params passthrough)
- crates/kyz-core/src/store.rs:1434 (unlock_to_dk parses attacker file)

## Remediation

Clamp on load in scrypt_params(): reject log_n outside 15..=20 and p outside 1..=8 (or compute the working area and reject above ~64 MiB) with a clear error before any scrypt call. Defaults (log_n=17, p=1) are inside these bounds, so existing and newly created vaults are unaffected; out-of-bounds files should be reported as corrupt.

## Proof of positive outcome (tests to write and run)

- Unit test (kyz-core vault_v3): scrypt_params with log_n=14, log_n=21, p=0, p=9 -> clean Err mentioning the bound; log_n=15..=20 with p=1..=8 -> Ok.
- Integration test: craft a v3 vault file with log_n=30 in a temp workspace; `kyz vault unlock` -> graceful error message, exit code != 134, no abort (assert exit code and stderr text).
- Regression: create + unlock a normal vault (log_n=17) still works.

description:
## Summary

Consolidated hardening backlog from the security audit (~/security-audit-skill/kyz/run-1/REPORT.md, run-1, 2026-08-29). These are defense-in-depth / hygiene items, NOT exploitable findings on their own:

1. CORS allow_origin(Any)/Any/Any on all kyz-api endpoints incl. GET /config (reveals alias/secret-ref names) — restrict origins or drop CORS for a localhost API. Enabler of the browser variant of trx-8yhb.
2. No rate limiting/lockout on POST /auth/approve — unlimited online passphrase oracle (~4 guesses/s/core measured, each burning scrypt CPU); unauthenticated request creation grows memory unboundedly (pending requests never cleaned until accessed).
3. --no-policy does not disable policy: resolve_policy returns the DEFAULT BLOCKING policy (fail-closed bug); policy.rs test_no_policy_allows_everything codifies the wrong behavior.
4. Audit logging writes to stderr; README claims syslog. Route to syslog/journald or add file sink (overlaps trx-e2dr audit-log facility).
5. IPC: ensure_secure_socket_parent chmods the parent of ANY user-specified --ipc-socket path to 0700 (destructive on shared dirs); socket is bind-then-chmod (brief world-connectable window); generate_request_id uses getrandom(...).unwrap_or_default() -> all-zero IDs on RNG failure would collide/overwrite in the store.
6. Data/state dirs created 0755 (metadata exposure only; files are 0600).
7. Vault writes non-atomic (fs::write, no temp+rename) — crash mid-write corrupts vault (data loss).
8. Fallback session encryption (no OS keyring) keyed by SHA-256(vault path|user|hostname) — observable values; acceptable only due to 0600/0700 placement; degrades to obfuscation if backups leak.

title: SECURITY(run-2 F6/MED): ensure_secure_socket_parent blind chmod — cross-user DoS, /tmp lockdown when run as root
close_reason: Fixed. ensure_secure_socket_parent refuses world-writable parents and verifies writability (ownership proxy, no unsafe) before chmod 0700. PoC rerun: root-owned dir, world-writable dir and /tmp (README example) all refused with clear errors; default state-dir socket works (0600).

title: SECURITY(run-2 F7/MED): wildcard CORS + opt-in auth exposes auth-request listing/deny/pickup to browser origins
close_reason: Fixed. Removed the wildcard CORS layer entirely; kyz-api fails closed without KYZ_API_TOKEN unless --insecure-no-auth is passed. PoC rerun: no access-control-allow-origin header, unauthenticated start refused, 401 without bearer / 200 with bearer.

title: SECURITY(run-2 F8/LOW): unbounded IPC read_line — same-UID memory-exhaustion DoS of whole daemon
close_reason: Fixed. IPC request line capped at 64 KiB, 10s read timeout, 64-connection semaphore. PoC rerun: 5x200KB newline-free flood leaves daemon healthy (health 200) and IPC functional.

title: SECURITY(run-2 F9/LOW): locked vault layer aborts LayeredVault resolution for later layers; empty path provenance
close_reason: Fixed. kyz-runtime resolver skips locked layers in resolve_in/resolve_strict and reports VaultLocked with the real layer path; mixed locked/unlocked integration test added.

title: kyz wrap exports vault master passphrase into wrapped child environment (KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD)
description:
## Summary

handle_wrap (crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:2446-2449) builds the wrapped child's environment via scrubbed_env() — which strips KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD — and then EXPLICITLY re-adds it: `child_env.push(("KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD".to_string(), passphrase))`. The wrapped process (the semi-trusted agent that kyz wrap exists to scope via --allow) can read the vault MASTER passphrase from its own env (os.environ, /proc/self/environ). It is inherited by every descendant and leaks into crash dumps / env-logging integrations.

## Impact (dynamically confirmed, v0.7.0)

`kyz wrap --allow github/token -- sh -c 'echo [$KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD]'` printed the full master passphrase. The passphrase decrypts the vault file OFFLINE and PERMANENTLY (backups, synced/git-committed workspace vaults) — strictly more powerful than the session DK the child legitimately holds. The vault is already unlocked before spawn (main.rs:2426, session DK in OS keyring), so the child never needs the passphrase for its approved access — the exposure is gratuitous. Baseline: aws-vault exec / op run / Vault Agent inject scoped revocable material, never the master credential.

## Affected code

- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:2449 (the re-add)
- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:2446 (scrubbed_env — defeated)
- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:2418-2423 (non-TTY passphrase read from env — the only legit consumer)

## Remediation

Delete line 2449. Nested kyz get/exec/set inside the wrap use the persisted session (keyring DK), not the passphrase. The ONLY functionality lost is a nested non-TTY `kyz wrap` (handle_wrap's own env read at :2421) — migrate that to a `kyz unlock --from-keyring` style helper if needed. Keep scrubbed_env() as the only source of child KYZ_* vars. Design direction already tracked in trx-2c3j.2 (brokered scoped-session API) — this fix is the immediate stopgap, independent of the broker design.

## Proof of positive outcome (tests to write and run)

- Integration test: run `kyz wrap --allow svc/key -- sh -c 'env'` (or printenv via a policy-allowed wrapper); assert KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD is ABSENT from child env; assert the wrapped command can still read the allowed secret via `kyz exec/pipe` (session-based path works).
- Regression test for non-TTY wrap: KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD=<pw> kyz wrap ... still works (env read at :2421 unchanged) but does NOT propagate the variable to grandchildren.
- Manual repro of the attack MUST fail: wrapped process printing its environ shows no vault passphrase.
close_reason: Fixed (run-1 F2). handle_wrap no longer re-adds KYZ_VAULT_PASSWORD to the child env; when a valid session exists the passphrase is not even requested. PoC rerun: wrapped child sees no passphrase; nested kyz exec inside wrap works via the keyring-backed session.

title: kyz exec: secret field names become injected env var names, enabling LD_PRELOAD/PATH code execution
description:
## Summary

resolve_exec_env (crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:1868-1875) and resolve_exec_env_headless (main.rs:2177-2178) convert each secret FIELD NAME to uppercase and inject it as an env var NAME=VALUE into the exec'd child (Command envs(&env) applied LAST at main.rs:2243-2247, overriding the scrubbed parent env). Field names have no allowlist/denylist — dynamic-loader and shell-hook variables (LD_PRELOAD, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, PATH, BASH_ENV, ...) are accepted. Policy checks (handle_exec:2230) inspect only the program basename, args, and --secret names — never the injected env var names; --tag/--alias-resolved entries escape even the secret-name check.

## Attack (dynamically confirmed, v0.7.0)

Poisoning primitive: a wrapped agent can `kyz set` (KYZ_NO_READ only gates get/export, main.rs:930/:1364) and `kyz import` deserializes untrusted JSON straight into SecretEntry with no field-name validation and no gate.

1. attacker: gcc -shared -fPIC -o /tmp/evil.so evil.c   (constructor payload)
2. attacker: kyz set ld --service pwn -f LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/evil.so
   (or: kyz set payload --service pwn -f PATH=/tmp/evilbin with a trojaned `id`)
3. victim: kyz exec --secret pwn/ld -- /bin/date
   -> "LD_PRELOAD constructor executed in child" (date never ran)
   victim: kyz exec --secret pwn/payload -- id -> attacker's script ran instead of /bin/id

--tag-based aliases mean the victim need not name the poisoned secret. Impact: arbitrary code execution in the user's exec context, where the vault session, keyring, and KYZ_API_TOKEN are reachable.

## Affected code

- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:1871-1875 (to_uppercase injection, interactive)
- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:2177-2178 (same, headless)
- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs:2243-2247 (sink: envs(&env).exec())
- crates/kyz-cli/src/main.rs handle_import:1406-1445 (ungated entry vector)

## Remediation

Allowlist env var names, checked on the UPPERACASED name: ^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$ plus a hard denylist (LD_*, DYLD_*, PATH, BASH_ENV, ENV, PYTHONSTARTUP, PYTHONPATH, IFS, ...). Apply the identical filter in resolve_exec_env_headless. Alternatively/in addition, require explicit `--env NAME=svc/key:field` mappings for every injected variable instead of deriving names from field names. Defense in depth: validate field names at `kyz set` and `kyz import` time.

## Proof of positive outcome (tests to write and run)

- Unit test on the new name filter: LD_PRELOAD, ld_preload, PATH, BASH_ENV, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, IFS -> rejected; VALUE, API_KEY, DB_HOST_1 -> accepted.
- Integration test: create secret with fields PATH=/tmp/x and LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/x and NOTE=ok; run `kyz exec --secret ... -- env` via a policy-allowed wrapper; assert PATH and LD_PRELOAD are NOT set in child (or exec hard-errors), NOTE=ok IS set.
- Same test through the headless path (KYZ_API_URL test server).
- Import test: `kyz import` of JSON with an LD_PRELOAD field name -> rejected with a clear error (or warnings), benign import unchanged.
- Manual repro of both original payloads MUST no longer achieve code execution.
close_reason: Fixed (run-1 F3). New kyz_core::is_safe_exec_env_name allowlist+denylist applied in both resolve_exec_env and resolve_exec_env_headless: field-derived names filtered with warning, explicit --env/alias names hard-error. PoC rerun: LD_PRELOAD/PATH poison fields skipped, real /bin/id ran, no hijack marker.

title: vault unlock: attacker-crafted KDF params (log_n/p) from vault file cause 1TiB allocation abort (DoS)
description:
## Summary

KdfParams (crates/kyz-core/src/vault_v3.rs:71-75) deserializes log_n: u8 and p: u32 straight from the vault file. scrypt_params (vault_v3.rs:105-114) applies no application-level bound before ScryptParams::new. Workspace vaults live at <repo>/.kyz/vault.json — attacker-controlled in a malicious cloned repo. When the victim runs `kyz vault unlock` there (ANY passphrase), derive_kek (vault_v3.rs:421-434) calls scrypt with attacker-chosen parameters.

## Impact (dynamically confirmed, v0.7.0)

log_n=30 / r=8 -> scrypt working area 128*8*2^30 = 1 TiB -> "memory allocation of 1099511627776 bytes failed" -> SIGABRT (exit 134). Without ulimits: OOM-killer pressure. Crash-DoS only. NOT a crypto downgrade: kdf params feed the KEK that AEAD-unwraps wrapped_dk — altering them on an existing vault makes unwrap_dk fail (AEAD tag check), so no offline brute-force speedup is reachable.

Repro: craft {"version":3,"kdf":{"algo":"scrypt","log_n":30,"r":8,"p":1,"salt_b64":"..."},"wrapped_dk":"...","entries":{}} at <repo>/.kyz/vault.json; cd repo; kyz vault unlock; enter any passphrase.

## Affected code

- crates/kyz-core/src/vault_v3.rs:71-75 (unvalidated log_n/p from file)
- crates/kyz-core/src/vault_v3.rs:105-114 (scrypt_params passthrough)
- crates/kyz-core/src/store.rs:1434 (unlock_to_dk parses attacker file)

## Remediation

Clamp on load in scrypt_params(): reject log_n outside 15..=20 and p outside 1..=8 (or compute the working area and reject above ~64 MiB) with a clear error before any scrypt call. Defaults (log_n=17, p=1) are inside these bounds, so existing and newly created vaults are unaffected; out-of-bounds files should be reported as corrupt.

## Proof of positive outcome (tests to write and run)

- Unit test (kyz-core vault_v3): scrypt_params with log_n=14, log_n=21, p=0, p=9 -> clean Err mentioning the bound; log_n=15..=20 with p=1..=8 -> Ok.
- Integration test: craft a v3 vault file with log_n=30 in a temp workspace; `kyz vault unlock` -> graceful error message, exit code != 134, no abort (assert exit code and stderr text).
- Regression: create + unlock a normal vault (log_n=17) still works.
close_reason: Fixed (run-1 F5). KdfParams::validate_params clamps log_n to 15..=20, r to 1..=64, p to 1..=8 before any scrypt call. PoC rerun: unlock of log_n=30 vault fails with a clean error, no allocation abort. Unit tests in audit_fix_tests.

title: auth-request flow: approved secrets stealable via unauthenticated one-time pickup URL
description:
## Summary

The kyz-api auth-request flow delivers human-approved secrets to whoever GETs /auth/secrets/{id} first. The stash is keyed ONLY by the request ID — no requester binding, no capability token. With KYZ_API_TOKEN unset (the DEFAULT deployment), auth_middleware passes every request, and GET /auth/request publicly lists ALL request IDs + scopes.

## Attack (dynamically confirmed against a local build, v0.7.0)

Attacker = any principal that can open TCP to 127.0.0.1:<port>: another local Unix user on a shared host, any co-located container sharing the netns (k8s pod sidecars), or a web page in the user's browser (CORS allow_origin(Any), subject to browser PNA):

1. GET /auth/request -> harvest pending request IDs + scopes (no auth)
2. websocat ws://127.0.0.1:3000/auth/wait/<id> -> notified the instant a human approves
3. human approves: POST /auth/approve/{id} with vault passphrase (only human action)
4. attacker GET /auth/secrets/{id} -> one-time pickup returns FULL plaintext values
5. legitimate requester's pickup -> 404 (stash consumed by attacker)

Observed: attacker received {"github/token":{"value":"ghp_SUPERSECRETVALUE123"}} without ever knowing the passphrase.

## Affected code

- crates/kyz-api/src/main.rs:147-156 (auth_middleware: no token -> pass all)
- crates/kyz-api/src/main.rs:221 (list_auth_requests: lists IDs/scopes unauthenticated)
- crates/kyz-api/src/main.rs:429-440 (pickup_secrets: no caller check)
- crates/kyz-core/src/auth_request.rs:143 (stash_secrets), :156 (pickup_secrets: remove-by-id)

Baseline: HashiCorp Vault response wrapping returns the single-use wrap token ONLY to the requester and never lists it; Teleport binds approval to the requesting identity. Bearer-URL pickup with a public listing is a deviation.

## Remediation

1. Add a client-generated high-entropy pickup capability (>=32 bytes) to CreateAuthRequest; store alongside the request; pickup_secrets(id, capability) removes the stash only on constant-time capability match — the ID alone is never sufficient.
2. Update kyz-cli submit_and_wait_auth_request (main.rs:2031-2036, 2090-2093) in the SAME change to generate the capability client-side and send it on pickup, or legit `kyz exec` headless flow breaks.
3. Stop listing request IDs to unauthenticated callers (or require the API token for GET /auth/request even in no-token mode).
4. Consider enabling bearer auth by default for everything except /health.

## Proof of positive outcome (tests to write and run)

- Unit test (kyz-core auth_request): create request with pickup_capability; pickup with wrong capability -> Err/None (stash retained or 401); pickup with correct capability -> values; second pickup -> None. Capability must NOT appear in any list() output.
- Integration test (kyz-api): spin up router with test state, POST /auth/request without capability -> 400 (or require field); with capability -> 201; GET /auth/secrets/{id} without capability -> 401; with wrong capability -> 401; with correct -> 200 + values; repeat -> 404.
- CLI integration test: headless exec flow (`kyz exec` with locked vault + KYZ_API_URL pointing at test server) completes end-to-end with capability auth (no regression).
- Manual repro of the original attack MUST now fail: list -> wait -> pickup returns 401 without the capability.

Related: trx-ymjw (audit log for auth requests/approvals), trx-gber (request expiry/cleanup).
close_reason: Fixed (run-1 F1). Requests now require a client-generated pickup_capability (>=32 chars) at creation; one-time pickup requires the capability (constant-time compared, never serialized/listed); missing/wrong capability is a uniform 404. CLI headless flow generates and presents it. PoC rerun: listing leaks nothing, no-capability pickup 404, correct capability 200, replay 404, create without capability 422.

title: Design: scoped secret sessions (wrap broker) compatible with oqto sandbox placements
Design: scoped secret sessions (wrap broker) compatible with oqto sandbox placements
description:
# Scoped Secret Sessions — wrap broker design (closes the enforcement half of trx-eyyz)

## Problem
`kyz wrap --allow X` must confine a semi-trusted agent to the named secrets. Env-var enforcement (KYZ_NO_READ) is child-mutable; a "scoped sub-session" in the OS keyring fails on Linux because the full-DK session sits in the same same-UID-readable collection. Principle: the decryption capability (DK) AND the scope check must live outside anything the child can inspect.

## Architecture: per-session broker (ssh-agent-proxy model)
- `kyz wrap` / embedder unlocks host-side, verifies refs, loads DK into a BROKER process only (no keyring entry, no session file, no env passphrase).
- Broker holds a GrantStore (existing jit.rs GrantScope: refs/commands/workspaces/expiry/use_count) and serves `GetSecret{ref, field}` over a Unix socket (line-JSON, same framing as kyz-api IPC).
- Child env carries only: KYZ_WRAP_SOCKET, KYZ_WRAP_TOKEN, KYZ_SESSION_MODE=wrap. All `kyz get/exec/pipe/export` calls route through the broker when these are set; a RuntimeContext SecretStore impl picks broker-backed vs keyring-backed.
- Broker sets PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0, daemonizes (Yama ptrace_scope=1 blocks sibling ptrace), dies with the child session / TTL — DK never touches disk and never survives the session (strictly better than keyring sessions).

## Bypass analysis (all fail)
env-unset → broker still scoped; raw kyz with cleared env → no keyring session exists → locked; steal socket+token → token only authorizes scoped requests; ptrace broker → Yama+dumpable mitigations (root defeats — accepted, documented); writes (set/delete/rollback) → refused by default (optional --writable later).

## Oqto placement compatibility (hard requirements)
R1 Unix-socket-first transport; TCP is never required (container placements may have isolated networks).
R2 Placement-neutral exposure: socket lives in oqto's per-session socket dir (already 0700 + bound into the sandbox, same dir the SSH proxy uses) or crosses container boundary via the existing /run/oqto bind-mount/endpoint-bridge pattern (ExposedEndpoint::Unix). No new transport invented.
R3 Auth by per-session token, NOT by UID/POSIX perms — container placements may run different UIDs across the socket.
R4 The sandbox NEVER needs vault or keyring access: the broker holds the DK host-side. This is also a coverage unlock — today's keyring-session model cannot serve container placements at all (no keyring/XDG inside); the broker is what makes kyz usable there.
R5 Scope enforcement is 100% broker-side. Sandbox path-hiding of vault/keyring is defense-in-depth only; when a placement cannot hide them, the gap MUST surface via oqto-sandbox's BackendCapabilities/OnMissingCapability (Fail/Warn/Ignore) convention — never silently weaker.
R6 Config mirrors the [ssh] section: a [kyz] block in sandbox.toml (global default + workspace override, tighten-only) mapping 1:1 onto GrantScope: allowed_refs, allowed_commands, allowed_workspaces, ttl, log_requests, prompt_unknown (v1: fail on unexpected refs).
R7 Embedding surface lives in kyz-runtime: broker spawn/supervise mirroring oqto's SshAgentProxy (struct owns Child + socket path, torn down at session end) + programmatic client. Oqto is the first embedder.
R8 Standalone parity: `kyz wrap` spawns the same broker when no embedder is present — one protocol, two supervisors.
R9 Remote-machine placements keep the existing kyz-api headless flow; IssueGrant/ValidateGrant already implement the same GrantStore semantics, so local broker and remote API converge on one scope model.

### Placement matrix
| Placement | Broker | Transport | Vault/keyring in sandbox | Guarantees |
| host + bwrap/landlock/seatbelt | host, per session | session socket dir (bound in) | hidden by path policy; gap declared if not | strongest |
| host, no sandbox (dev) | host | session socket dir | visible → declared Warn gap | scope still enforced (broker-side) |
| container | host-side, runner-supervised | bind-mounted Unix socket (/run/oqto) | absent entirely | strongest + placement coverage unlock |
| remote machine | kyz-api (host) | existing HTTP approval flow | n/a | same GrantStore semantics |

## Rollout
P1: broker protocol + kyz-runtime client/broker (refs+TTL scope), standalone `kyz wrap` rewired, bypass test suite (every row of the bypass table as a test).
P2: [kyz] sandbox.toml section in oqto_refactor; --command/--workspace constraints; nested-wrap narrowing (inner allow must be subset of outer); broker audit log (allowed/denied ref + command basename — today in-wrap reads are invisible).
P3: Landlock/seatbelt hardening declared through the capability model; --writable; Windows transport (named pipes).

## Open questions
- Container placements: runner-supervised broker (embed kyz-runtime in oqto-runner, like the endpoint bridges) vs exec'ing kyz CLI — recommend runner-embedded.
- prompt_unknown-style interactive approval for out-of-scope refs (like [ssh] prompt_unknown) — v1 fails closed.
